{"path":"snake_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html","edit_description":"
Replace the stub content with a COMPLETE, self-contained classic Snake game (HTML+CSS+JS all in this one file). Requirements:

GRID & CORE MECHANICS:
- 30x30 grid rendered on an HTML canvas (each cell e.g. 18-20px, canvas size ~560-600px square), centered on the page.
- Snake moves continuously in one of four directions (up/down/left/right) at a fixed tick interval (e.g. setInterval or requestAnimationFrame with accumulator, ~100-120ms per move).
- Snake grows by one segment each time it eats a food item; food respawns at a random empty cell not occupied by any snake.
- Game ends (for a given snake) if it hits a wall (goes outside 0..29 in x or y) or collides with any part of its own body or the other snake's body (when two snakes are present). Track and display which player/snake lost.
- Score = number of food items eaten (or length-based score) displayed live during gameplay for each active snake.

MODES (selectable from a start menu before playing):
1. Human vs Human: two snakes, Snake A controlled with Arrow Keys, Snake B controlled with WASD. Both are human controlled.
2. CPU vs Human: one snake human controlled (Arrow Keys), one snake CPU controlled.
3. CPU vs CPU: both snakes CPU controlled, purely a simulation.
Support a single-snake human-only classic mode too if natural (optional extra), but the 3 required modes must be selectable via clickable menu buttons or number key selection in the start menu.

CPU AI:
- CPU-controlled snake(s) automatically search for the nearest/current food using a simple pathfinding approach (e.g. greedy BFS/shortest-path on the grid avoiding walls and snake bodies, falling back to a safe random/greedy direction if no path found so it doesn't immediately suicide into a wall or body when possible).
- CPU logic runs every tick before moving.

CONTROLS:
- Arrow keys move snake A (or the sole human snake).
- WASD move snake B when human vs human mode is active.
- Keyboard controls must prevent reversing directly into the snake's own body (can't go from moving right directly to left in one tick).
- Preserve default browser scrolling prevention for arrow keys/wasd during gameplay (preventDefault on keydown).

SCREENS / UI:
- Start menu screen shown on load: title "Snake", mode selection buttons (Human vs Human / CPU vs Human / CPU vs CPU), brief instructions (controls per mode), and a "Press Enter or click Start to begin" prompt.
- Gameplay screen: canvas with the grid, score(s) displayed above or beside canvas (label each snake, e.g. "Player 1: 3" and "Player 2 / CPU: 5").
- Game over screen: shown when the game ends; display final score(s) and result (winner / who crashed / draw if simultaneous), and text "Press Enter/Space to restart" or "Press M to return to menu".
- Restarting: pressing Enter or Space on the game-over screen restarts the SAME mode; pressing a key like 'M' (or a visible button) returns to the start menu to pick a new mode.

VISUAL STYLE:
- Clean modern dark-theme CSS: dark background, colored snake segments (distinct colors per snake), distinct food color, grid lines subtle or a simple border, centered layout, nice readable fonts, a bit of styling on buttons.
- Everything (HTML structure, CSS in a <style> tag, JS in a <script> tag) must be in this single HTML file — no external file references, no CDN links.

CODE QUALITY:
- Well-structured vanilla JavaScript, no frameworks/libraries.
- Use requestAnimationFrame with a timestamp-based accumulator for the game loop so speed is consistent, or setInterval — either is fine as long as movement is smooth and consistent.
- Handle edge cases: don't let a food spawn on top of a snake; when a snake dies mid-game in a two-snake mode, stop updating that snake but let the game continue until the game-ending condition is met (both dead, or one dead in a mode where that ends the whole match) — simplest robust rule: the match ends as soon as ANY snake dies (wall or self or other-snake collision), showing that as game over with a clear message of which snake died and the scores; this is simplest and acceptable.
- No console errors, valid HTML5 doctype, meta charset, meta viewport for responsiveness.

Produce the entire file content now, fully working, replacing the current placeholder stub.
"}
